# What Ask Yoda answer-quality gaps are visible from recent history, logs, feedback, and retrieval behavior?

## Answer
Visible Ask Yoda answer-quality gaps from recent history (as reflected in logs/automation behavior, feedback plumbing, and retrieval behavior) cluster into: (1) failures to return an answer at all, (2) degraded/partial evidence when retrieval times out, and (3) (still) limited observability tying a given answer to what retrieval actually happened.

### 1) Availability gap: evaluator/log history shows requests can hang long enough that automated quality evaluation can’t complete
A recent Daily Learning Intake evaluator run failed to produce a snapshot because it got stuck waiting on an Ask Yoda HTTPS response (`urlopen(...).getresponse()` blocked) and had to be interrupted. This is a direct “no answer returned” quality gap because it prevents both user answers and automated answer-quality assessment. [reports/memory-stargraph-daily-learning-intake-2026-07-29-bounded-85]

Even though the evaluator snapshot failed, synthetic/test Ask Yoda records were still captured in `data/yoda_logs.json` and exposed via `/api/yoda-logs`, implying the system can record attempts while still failing to reliably complete request/response cycles. [reports/memory-stargraph-daily-learning-intake-2026-07-29-bounded-85]

### 2) Retrieval degradation gap: broad-graph retrieval can time out, leading to missing evidence unless the degraded-path is explicit and bounded
A recurring issue is that “broad graph traversal” (optional context expansion) can consume the full configured timeout on cold stable-context retrieval, yielding >1 minute waits even when model generation is ~9 seconds. This creates a quality gap because answers may either arrive too late to be usable or must proceed without broad evidence. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/bound-ask-yoda-broad-graph-retrieval-latency]

The intended durable behavior is to treat broad graph traversal as optional and bounded, while still preserving core evidence (selected-node, backlink checks, question-specific search, targeted relationship evidence) when broad retrieval times out. The need to explicitly preserve this evidence reveals that, historically, answers can lose important supporting context under timeout pressure. [learnings/memory-stargraph-bounded-broad-context-tail-latency-2026-07-17]

A dedicated TODO exists to reduce the “recurring broad-graph timeout regression” for evaluator workloads and to ensure diagnostics distinguish “optional broad-graph timeout” from “missing evidence” and from hard retrieval failures—indicating that recent behavior still produces answer-quality ambiguity when broad retrieval degrades. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/reduce-recurring-ask-yoda-broad-graph-timeout-regression]

### 3) Retrieval-thoroughness gap: answers can be too local to the selected node unless search/backlinks/direct reads are used
A completed retrieval-thoroughness effort exists specifically because answers were previously “limited to the selected node or immediate graph neighborhood,” and needed targeted search, graph expansion, backlink checks, and direct reads to find relevant material outside the immediate neighborhood. The existence of this remediation implies that recent history contained gaps where answers missed relevant sources not adjacent to the starting node. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/enhance-ask-yoda-retrieval-thoroughness]

### 4) Observability/attribution gap: users (and operators) can’t always tell whether poor answer quality is due to missing knowledge vs retrieval timeouts vs tool failures
Multiple completed diagnostics-focused efforts indicate that recent Ask Yoda history included cases where it was difficult to understand why answers failed or degraded.

Ask Yoda latency and context construction became dominant enough that existing timing was “too coarse” to identify whether graph traversal, backlinks, search, direct reads, or repeated stable context was responsible. This is an answer-quality gap because without phase-level attribution, it’s hard to know whether an answer is incomplete due to skipped/failed retrieval steps. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/profile-and-reduce-ask-yoda-prompt-context-latency]

A separate completed item notes that persisted View Log data dropped key cache-hit/subphase/context-count fields needed to diagnose cold-path latency and whether a context cache contributed, again obscuring the link between retrieval behavior and the resulting answer. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/persist-yoda-context-diagnostics-and-reduce-cold-path-latency]

The View Log diagnostics expansion explicitly targets explaining “what went wrong when Ask Yoda fails or degrades,” including timeout vs other failures, fallback usage, request_id/source, timing phases, selected slug/depth, and model output status. The need for this indicates that recent failures/degradations were not self-explanatory from the logs/UI, making answer-quality regressions harder to interpret. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/improve-ask-yoda-view-log-diagnostics]

### 5) Feedback gap (quality signal capture, not correctness): feedback exists and is durable, but the provided excerpts don’t show what it says about answer quality yet
A feedback loop was implemented so users can rate every completed answer (thumbs up/down) and leave text feedback, persisted durably and separated from chat history. This closes a prior gap in collecting answer-quality signals, but the excerpts here don’t include actual feedback content/metrics, so no specific answer-quality failure modes can be enumerated from feedback itself. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/implement-ask-yoda-user-feedback-loop] [runs/memory-stargraph-wish-20260717t085001-0700-82cb62fc-b001] [learnings/memory-stargraph-durable-yoda-feedback-ledger-2026-07-17]

### 6) Presentation/synthesis gap (partly addressed): answers previously surfaced raw retrieval output rather than a synthesized response
A completed effort exists because Ask Yoda “currently surfaces raw query/retrieval output” and needed to use retrieved context internally and return a concise conversational answer instead. The presence of this change indicates a recent history gap where answer quality (readability/usability) suffered from exposing scaffolding rather than synthesis. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/refine-ask-yoda-answers-with-model]

## Gaps
- Recent actual user feedback contents/aggregates (thumb up/down rates, common negative themes, example comments) tied to answer IDs, so we can name concrete answer-quality failure modes from feedback rather than only from infrastructure notes. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/implement-ask-yoda-user-feedback-loop] [learnings/memory-stargraph-durable-yoda-feedback-ledger-2026-07-17]
- Concrete recent View Log samples (for real user sessions) showing specific retrieval sequences (selected-node/search/backlinks/direct reads/broad traversal) vs the final answer quality, to quantify which retrieval behavior correlates with which quality gaps. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/improve-ask-yoda-view-log-diagnostics] [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/persist-yoda-context-diagnostics-and-reduce-cold-path-latency]
- The interrupted evaluator run’s per-question outcomes (which questions were asked, which hung, which succeeded, whether any returned degraded contexts) since the snapshot file was not written. [reports/memory-stargraph-daily-learning-intake-2026-07-29-bounded-85]



## Gaps
- Recent actual user feedback contents/aggregates (thumb up/down rates, common negative themes, example comments) tied to answer IDs.
- Concrete recent View Log samples (real user sessions) showing retrieval sequence (selected-node/search/backlinks/direct reads/broad traversal) mapped to final answer quality.
- The interrupted evaluator run’s per-question outcomes and any partial snapshot/error details beyond the hang description (since no snapshot file was written).

# Where could synthetic resolver, Ask Yoda, or worker probes contaminate production feedback or hide user-facing quality problems?

## Answer

### 1) Synthetic resolver “verification traffic” can be recorded as production learning/feedback
A known contamination path is resolver verification traffic being stored as **production / non-synthetic / non-test** due to missing or incorrect classification. This happened during V1.0.145 verification traffic (about 02:31–02:35 America/Los_Angeles) and triggered a requirement to re-audit all probe paths and prove production/test separation is live. [notes/memory-starmap-todo-list/separate-synthetic-resolver-probe-telemetry]

Related durable boundary: test harnesses must not silently inherit a live telemetry bridge (i.e., external resolver delivery must be suppressed by default unless explicitly doing an integration/live verification). If violated, synthetic runs can leak into the same resolver/telemetry stream used for production learning. [learnings/memory-stargraph-synthetic-telemetry-boundary-2026-07-16]

### 2) Resolver event pipeline normalization/readback can erase the distinction (or hide it)
Memory Stargraph’s `/api/entity-ask-yoda` path submits events with `environment`, `synthetic`, `test_run`, and `pair_id`, and `/api/resolver/events` “normalizes those fields for readback.” If normalization is wrong or collapses values, it can (a) mix synthetic into production feedback views, or (b) make it look like production is healthy by filtering/mislabeling problematic production events as synthetic (or vice-versa). [reports/memory-stargraph-sre-weekly-resilience-recovery-2026-07-28-f62a12e]

### 3) Ask Yoda evaluator logs can look like real user feedback unless explicitly split
There is an explicit product lesson that **production learning must default to production feedback only**, while synthetic/test feedback should be auditable only through an explicit include-test path and split counts. If any dashboard/report/learning job uses the “include-test” path by default (or fails to split counts), synthetic Ask Yoda feedback could contaminate production quality signals and bury real user-facing problems in noise. [learnings/memory-stargraph-durable-yoda-feedback-ledger-2026-07-17]
